title: [Run] Synchronize settings file read/write
author: dsrivastavv
summary: PowerToys Run can receive multiple settings-file watcher callbacks while Settings is writing settings.json, and its reader still retries around a writer-held file lock.
next_action: Instrument one settings change and verify callback count, lock retries, and UI-thread work before approving a synchronization design.

confidence.rationale: The current source explicitly preserves the reported synchronization TODO.

judgment.rationale: The old issue's synchronization concern is still visible in current SettingsReader: a file watcher calls ReadSettings and the IOException path explicitly says proper synchronization with Settings remains needed.
evidence: The issue describes runner IPC writing settings.json followed by repeated PowerLauncher FileWatcher callbacks.
Current SettingsReader.ReadSettingsOnChange registers a watcher callback that immediately calls ReadSettings.
Current IOException handling comments that the Settings app can hold the file lock and should be properly synchronized instead of retried.
judgment.recommended_action: Instrument one settings change and verify callback count, lock retries, and UI-thread work before approving a synchronization design.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current source confirms the debt, but a lightweight pass did not inspect the writer transaction or establish whether debounce, atomic replacement, or IPC acknowledgement is the correct fix boundary.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run can receive multiple settings-file watcher callbacks while Settings is writing settings.json, and its reader still retries around a writer-held file lock.
known_information: The issue is a maintainer-authored code-quality bug.
Current reader has an in-process read lock and retry loop.
The synchronization TODO remains in public source.
inferences: Multiple watcher notifications and transient file locks may still cause redundant reads, but their current user impact is not measured.
issue_context.analysis: The issue remains technically grounded, but the next useful action is a targeted current trace rather than an unverified implementation plan.
initial_investigation: Confirmed the watcher callback and synchronization TODO remain.

actions.label: Trace PowerToys Run settings reload
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Measure settings watcher callbacks and lock retries
prerequisites: Debug or trace-capable current PowerToys build
setup: Enable logging around SettingsReader.ReadSettingsOnChange and ReadSettings retry count.
steps: Change one PowerToys Run setting in Settings.
Count file watcher callbacks for that one logical update.
Record whether reads encounter IOException or JSON retry paths.
Confirm whether callbacks execute serially and whether visible Run state updates once.
reproduce.expected_result: One logical settings update should produce one coherent runtime update without lock-related retries or repeated UI work.
